lines.name: Marine Environment Protection Authority
lines.rationale: Only national agency involved in monitoring, regulating and acting to minimize impact of oil spills and shipping activity on marine environment, which is highly important in the context of Sri Lanka's role as a maritime hub and the impacts of the 2021 X-press Pearl Disaster
lines.source: BER 2015-2024 Dataset .xlsx, sheet OASigBE Exp

lines.name: Central Environment Authority
lines.rationale: Main national agency mandated with providing Environment Impact Assessment (EIAs) on major development and investment projects, while also setting the standards and regulation of industrial waste disposal, municipal waste management, hazardous waste management, with direct relevance to biodiversity
lines.source: BER 2015-2024 Dataset .xlsx, sheet OASigBE Exp

lines.name: Sri Lanka Customs Biodiversity, Culture & National Heritage Protection Division
lines.rationale: Unit within Sri Lanka Customs that implemented the National Biodiversity Framework for Cartegena Protocol for Biosafety at the border. Expenditure shared with us is only those relevant to this implementation, hence the 100% relevance, eventhough the unit as a whole has other mandates.
lines.source: BER 2015-2024 Dataset .xlsx, sheet OASigBE Exp

lines.name: National Aquaculture Development Authority
lines.rationale: Sustainable livelihoods for fisheries, especially lagoons and inland water bodies, through sustainable methods is the biodiversity relevant activity. While division wise data is not avaialable, reading of annual reports of NAQDA indicates that this aspect only covers about 1% of the authorities overall activity.
lines.source: BER 2015-2024 Dataset .xlsx, sheet OAMarBE Exp

lines.name: Mahaweli Authority of Sri Lanka
lines.rationale: 2016 to 2021 Annual Reports of MASL provides division wise expenditure breakdowns, allowing us to identify the expenditure of only the divisions with Biodiversity relevant mandates - River Basin Management Office, Water Management Secretariat, Land Use Planning Division and Environment & Forest Conservation Division. For 2015 and 2022-2024, values based on the trend and average for 2016-2021 were utilized.
lines.source: BER 2015-2024 Dataset .xlsx, sheet OAMarBE Exp

lines.name: Department of Animal Production and Health
lines.rationale: Wildlife health surveillaince and biosafety aspects are what is biodiversity relevant. Division wise expenditure is not available, so reasonable assumption of 7% taken to reflect assumptions of previous BER report and narrative in DAPH annual reports.
lines.source: BER 2015-2024 Dataset .xlsx, sheet OAMarBE Exp

lines.name: Department of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources
lines.rationale: Fisheries management and illegal fishing activity prevention to reduce overfishing and damage to marine environment are what is biodiversity relevant. Division wise expenditure is not available, so reasonable assumption of 7% taken to reflect assumptions of previous BER report and narrative in DFAR annual reports.
lines.source: BER 2015-2024 Dataset .xlsx, sheet OAMarBE Exp

lines.name: Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation
lines.rationale: 1 of 8 activity divisions is Wetland Management Division which helps restore and manage urban wetlands, including dedicated wetland nature parks. While division wise expenditure is not available, SLLDC's largest projects are relevant to flood control and management according to its annual report, allowing us to make a reasonable assumption of only 4% expenditure for biodiversity relevant wetland conservation activity
lines.source: BER 2015-2024 Dataset .xlsx, sheet OAMarBE Exp

lines.name: Coast Conservation and Coastal Resource Management Department
lines.rationale: Annual reports of CCCRMD provided a breakdown of key project expenditure and we identified as biodiversity relevant programs on Education & Awareness, removing illegal coastal constructions, testing water pollution levels in outlets to sea, surveys of coastal environment and seabed. On top of that we assumed some extent of administrative expenses relevant to these aspects, allowing us to provide expenditure shares that vary across the years.
lines.source: BER 2015-2024 Dataset .xlsx, sheet OAMarBE Exp

lines.name: National Aquatic Resources Research and Development Agency
lines.rationale: Annual reports of NARA indicated that on average about 15% of their expenditure was on research activity with relevance to biodiversity and ecosystems
lines.source: BER 2015-2024 Dataset .xlsx, sheet OAMarBE Exp

notes: The review's total counts institutions: the four core biodiversity agencies and the dedicated units in full, other agencies at the relevance rate the review states for each.

The review's project lines are a second view of the same money, each at its own weight; many sit inside the institutions above, so the two are never added. The policy areas are read from the project lines, where the review's tags sit.
All government spending is the series the review labels total primary expenditure; it equals the Ministry of Finance's total expenditure, interest included (2023: LKR 5,357 billion).
US$ figures use the review's own annual average rates; in US$ the series falls after the 2022 devaluation while it rises in rupees.
The dedicated units' 2024 figure is a single estimate of LKR 120 million, not broken down by unit; Sri Lanka Customs has no figures for 2022-2024 and the Land Development Corporation none for 2024.

Project rows 45 and 71 appear to be the same World Bank project (ecosystem conservation and management) under two titles: equal amounts in 2018 and 2019 and LKR 203.4 against 203.431 million in 2017, LKR 1,896.6 million in all. The review counts both, as does the record; the pair is flagged for the review team to confirm.
